niche_preference_profile: Prefers interfaces that feel complete, structured, and intentionally composed, with strong hierarchy, clear sectioning, and high scanability. They consistently like polished, production-ready screens with visible content and actionable controls rather than sparse or unfinished layouts. Their taste often favors restrained modern UI: balanced spacing, coherent grouping, subtle containment, and reduced clutter. They also repeatedly respond well to calm, muted palettes, soft rounded geometry, and integrated search/controls, though their brightness and mood preferences vary by context between airy light minimalism and sleek dark premium treatments.

criteria.description: Prefers screens that look fully built-out, finished, and production-ready, with no empty, stray, placeholder-like, or unresolved areas.
Prefers explicit multi-section organization with labeled groups, strong structural separation, and a screen architecture that makes categories easy to understand.
Prefers strong top-down hierarchy with clear emphasis, easy vertical scanning, and distinct informational flow rather than mixed or competing priorities.
Prefers fewer competing regions, less visual noise, and simpler compositions that avoid unnecessary decorative or functional competition.
Prefers even, disciplined vertical spacing and repeated visual cadence rather than abrupt gaps, drift, or uneven pacing between modules.
Prefers layouts where elements feel naturally integrated into one coherent page flow, rather than isolated modules, detached inserts, or disconnected regions.
Prefers interfaces with clearly visible actions, obvious affordances, and enough on-screen functionality to feel immediately usable for the task.
Prefers polished, contemporary interfaces with controlled styling and intentional composition rather than experimental, generic, or rough-looking presentation.
Prefers soft rounded cards, pills, and containers with gentle modern edges, as long as the geometry feels cohesive rather than bulky or puffy.
Prefers accent colors and icon treatments used in a controlled, balanced way, avoiding overly loud, competing, or excessive emphasis.
Prefers search fields, toggles, consent controls, and navigation elements that sit naturally within the layout instead of feeling pasted on or overly dominant.
Prefers content-first screens where decorative imagery, hero treatments, and ornamental effects do not overpower the functional information.
Prefers conventional, legible navigation cues and drill-down affordances that make interaction options obvious and grounded.
Prefers one dominant action or focal path at a time rather than split decisions, competing buttons, or multiple equally prominent controls.
Prefers components, alerts, and modals that remain visibly anchored within a larger app screen, preserving surrounding context and realism.
Prefers concise, direct, matter-of-fact copy and clearly framed information over procedural clutter, vague marketing language, or overly ornamental phrasing.
Prefers headers that support hierarchy cleanly without excessive chrome, competing branding, or fragmented top-of-screen elements.
